purpose: Ertapenem is a strong antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections in different parts of the body, such as the stomach, lungs, skin, urinary tract, and pelvis. It is also used to prevent infections after certain surgeries. Your doctor will prescribe this when other antibiotics may not be strong enough.
how_it_works: Ertapenem works by attacking the outer wall that surrounds bacteria. Without this wall, the bacteria cannot survive and they die off. Because it targets the bacterial wall and not your own cells, it is able to fight the infection while being safe for your body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include diarrhea, nausea, headache, and redness or swelling at the injection site. Some people may also experience vomiting, low blood pressure, or a mild rash. Let your doctor or pharmacist know if any of these bother you.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to penicillin, cephalosporins, or any other antibiotics, as you may also be allergic to ertapenem. In rare cases, it can cause serious allergic reactions or seizures, especially if you have kidney problems or a history of seizures. It can also cause a serious gut infection called C. difficile, which causes severe diarrhea — contact your doctor right away if this happens. Always tell your healthcare team about all your medications before starting this drug.
typical_dosing: Ertapenem is given as an injection either into a vein (IV) or into a muscle (IM), usually once a day. The standard adult dose is 1 gram per day. The length of treatment depends on your infection but typically lasts 3 to 14 days. This medication is usually given by a healthcare professional in a clinic or hospital setting.
